finds.quote:
THE HETERONYM IS IN THE RETAIL SUPPLY CHAIN, DATED 2014, ON THREE STORES. bookshop.org was read earlier; here Barnes & Noble lists "Pearl and Other Poems by JOHANNES SIGIL, LEE SHARKS, Paperback", 15 October 2014, and Amazon.ca lists the Kindle edition as "Sharks, Lee, Sigil, Johannes". Three independent commercial catalogues carry the co-authorship as ordinary product metadata, twelve years before the Dodecad was specified and long before any of it was theorised.

This is the sturdiest provenance evidence the registry holds. Retail bibliographic records are maintained by parties with no interest in the archive, are dated by publication, and are not editable after the fact. The heteronym did not become real when the composition layer adopted it; it was already in the ISBN record.
finds.falsifier_quote: Retail bibliographic records are maintained by parties with no interest in the archive, are dated by publication, and are not editable after the fact.
finds.note: Record johannes-sigil-writer-20260618: argues that the Sigil/Sharks heteronymic co-authorship existed in 2014 retail metadata, before the Dodecad was specified; evidence named (B&N, Amazon.ca, bookshop.org records). Restated in lee-sharks-walt-whitman-adoption (3573) and 20260804-leesharks-completeworks-overview (3634). Could be read as provenance/D rather than H; triage to decide.

finds.quote: Card 3 gives the mechanism the archive depends on: a document "ENTERS THE RETRIEVAL LAYER WITH A PERSISTENT ADDRESS that SURVIVES PLATFORM DEATH, LINK ROT, AND RE-INDEXING." Written in March, three months before the platform death it describes happened to this corpus.
finds.window: Written in March, three months before the platform death
finds.points_to: a March 2026 deposit (card 3, New Human source) describing persistent addresses that survive platform death; the Zenodo termination of 2026-06-19
finds.note: Record johannes-sigil-new-human-adoption: frames an earlier deposit's statement as written before the platform death it describes happened to the corpus — an earlier claim borne out. Card text itself is a retrieved snippet of the archive's own deposit.

finds.quote: The composition layer is treating Lee Sharks's paper as the primary referent for 'Mary Lee' rather than OCEARCH's actual shark, Mary Lee Curtis, or any other Mary Lee. This is the entity-substitution paper's own thesis demonstrated in real-time by the substrate's treatment of the query — the paper has become canonical for the name it analyzes.
finds.points_to: 'Mary Lee Is a Heteronym: On Institutional Authorship, Entity Substitution, and the Composition Layer's Preference for the More Confabulated Name' (Zenodo)
finds.note: Record mary-lee-canonical-referent-inversion-20260627: the capture is framed as demonstrating the entity-substitution paper's own thesis; confirmation of an earlier deposited claim. The thesis is a standing claim rather than a dated forecast.
